title: Why Philippine agriculture needs more than higher yields

blocks.text: Philippine agriculture stands at a critical crossroads as it confronts shrinking farm sizes, rising production costs, climate change, weak market integration and increasing dependence on imported food and agricultural technologies. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority’s 2022 Census of Agriculture and Fisheries show that average farm size declined from 3.61 hectares in 1970 to 0.82 hectare in 2022, limiting economies of scale and reducing farmer competitiveness. At the same time, farmers face rising costs for fertilizers, fuel, machinery and transportation, while stronger typhoons, prolonged droughts, floods and other climate-related events threaten production stability.
